gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Audio Science Review (NTTY) bench-tested the FiiO DM13. That test found 0.0015% THD+N, 98 dB dynamic range and 10 h of battery life, and the player passed physical dropout test discs up to 3 mm. That makes it the only candidate whose skip resistance and runtime anyone has measured.
standout_why: I opened five of the rival pages. rottenwifi.com and macmyths.com say outright that their picks were not tested and quote only advertised anti-skip seconds (Jensen 60/120 s, GPX 40/100 s). howtovr.com and trettitre.com give only maker battery and power claims. theproductanalyst.com lists the DM13 with specs but no runtime or measurements. None of these five mentions Audio Science Review or names who measured anything. I could not read av.com (403), esquire.com (fetch blocked) or loudersound.com (truncated), so I can't rule out a measurement on those three.
decides: This backs the FiiO DM13 as the pick for someone who will carry the player around. It is the only candidate with a named lab result on skip resistance (dropout test discs) and on battery life (10 h on the ASR bench). Rivals only repeat buffer seconds from the box. Two cautions apply. First, ASR tested the non-Bluetooth DM13, so nothing has been measured on the Bluetooth link of the DM13 BT. Second, runtime reports for the DM13 run from just over 8 h (HomeTheaterHifi) to 10 h (ASR). The table should say '8–10 h measured, by source' rather than '~8 h'.

findings.label: THD+N, balanced output
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review
findings.note: NTTY (Flo), ASR reviewer. Posted 2025-02-07, edited 2026-09-09 to add firmware V17 results. Test tone 999.91 Hz, no dither. The review says the result is the same at 5 Vrms. Unit tested is the non-Bluetooth DM13.

findings.label: Maximum balanced output voltage
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review
findings.note: NTTY did not test the single-ended output. Channel imbalance measured 0.17 dB.

findings.label: Dynamic range
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review
findings.note: -60 dBFS tone without dither. A CD (16-bit) tops out around 96–98 dB, so this is at the format limit. Crosstalk measured -116 dBr at 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz.

findings.label: Battery runtime, measured
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review
findings.note: NTTY wrote: 'The batteries lasted 10 hours, as advertised, during my tests.' Volume, output and load are not stated.

findings.label: Disc-defect / skip resistance, measured
findings.value: Passes dropouts up to 3 mm (text also mentions 4 mm), back-to-back 2× 3 mm dropouts, 1.5–1.7 µm track pitch, 1.20–1.40 m/s linear velocity, 2–18% HF asymmetry
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review
findings.note: Uses test discs with built-in defects, which shows how well the drive reads damaged discs. It is not a shake test. NTTY says ESP on or off made no difference. Start-up from disc insertion to playback was 12–14 s.

findings.label: Battery runtime, reviewer use
findings.value: a little more than 8 h per charge
findings.source_title: FiiO DM13 Portable CD Player Review – Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity
findings.note: Mel Martin, 2025-02-05. Informal: the reviewer recorded hours over normal use, with no stated volume or load. The review says the reviewer listened over Bluetooth, but gives no latency or range figures.

findings.label: Battery runtime, reviewer estimate
findings.value: about 7–8 h under heavy use (12 h rated)
findings.source_title: Shanling EC Play Review – Mobile Audiophile
findings.note: Chris Love, 2026-07-04. The reviewer says 'I have no hard-line test to provide you', so this is an estimate, not a timed test. Anti-skip was checked by shaking the unit ('no skips'), with no method given.
